forks.ownership: Dalvik.ThreadState owns the objects as HOST-DEX VM state. Bionic.PthreadCondition owns the state machine. Guest ABI is not involved.
forks.locked_decision_impact: Does not reopen D002 or D008. Reads the plan sentence that keys futex by guest address as the guest pthread adapter, which that sentence does not explicitly limit.
forks.missing_authority: A consumer-binding record that names the host storage identity, cites this exact crossing, and does not widen production_scope.
forks.migration_impact: A later ThreadState port could call the closed operations on host-owned words. Guest pthread callers stay on the existing guest-word binding.

basis: agr_bionic_sync defines the pthread object as one in-guest 32-bit word
The pthread plan preserves Bionic object representation and keys futex wait/wake by guest address
No locked exemption removes VM-internal pthread objects from that rule
forks.ownership: The word remains guest-addressed Bionic state. Using it from HOST-DEX either moves VM state into guest VMA or changes that representation rule.
forks.locked_decision_impact: Putting the VM lock in guest VMA changes the host/guest ownership in D002. Changing the word rule changes the Bionic port contract.
forks.bionic_contract_change: Required unless the objects are placed in guest VMA, which is itself a new ownership decision.
forks.missing_authority: An explicit decision to place these objects in guest VMA, or an explicit change to the Bionic address contract. Neither exists.
forks.migration_impact: The ThreadState port cannot consume the crossing until that decision. The guest ABI or the Bionic contract would change.
